bullets.title: AI Safety 'Pacing' Narrative Hammers Semis, Lifts Software Defensively
bullets.body: Anthropic CEO Amodei's weekend call to slow frontier AI model development (joined by Altman and Musk) triggered a broad semi selloff: NVDA -3%, MU/SNDK/INTC/AMD -5%, CRWV/NBIS -7% pre-market. Software names rallied defensively (NOW +5%, CRM +3-4%, ADBE +2.4%) while Jefferies warns semis face multi-year de-rating risk if capex slows. Consensus view from multiple desks: knee-jerk reaction, not a fundamental spending reversal—AI buildout remains early and Amodei explicitly said pacing ≠ halting training.

bullets.title: NVDA: In Talks as ~$10B Anchor Investor in Anthropic IPO at ~$2T Valuation
bullets.body: Reuters reported NVDA is considering investing up to $10B as anchor investor in Anthropic's upcoming Nasdaq IPO targeting ~$100B raise at ~$2T valuation. Anthropic told investors it achieved positive adjusted operating income for the second consecutive quarter with gross margins above 80%. OpenAI CEO Altman separately confirmed the company will not IPO in 2026 due to safety concerns.

bullets.title: AAPL: iPhone 18 Pro/Max Week-1 Lead Times Sharply Shorter YoY; Demand Question Open
bullets.body: Multiple trackers (JPM, Hedgeye, JPM Chips for Breakfast) flag iPhone 18 Pro lead times averaging 7-19 days globally vs. 15-24 days for iPhone 17 series. China shows the sharpest YoY shortfall (13/21 days vs. 30/30 days). Hedgeye is short, citing zero lead times even on 2TB Pro Max; JPM (OW, $340 PT) cautions that supply allocation differs YoY and some demand is likely displaced to foldable Duo (pre-orders Oct 16).

bullets.title: ORCL: Ellison Cancels $7.5B Stock Sale; $684B Backlog Intact
bullets.body: Larry Ellison cancelled his 10b5-1 plan to sell up to 50M ORCL shares (~$7.5B), with no shares sold—signaling confidence in the outlook. ORCL carries a $684B contracted backlog, and cloud infrastructure revenue surged 121% YoY to $7.4B last quarter. GS Communacopia conference showed strong investor sentiment on the name.

bullets.title: RBLX: Developer Conference Shows AI Tools + Roblox Everywhere = Path to 1B DAUs
bullets.body: JPM (Neutral) and GS both incrementally constructive post-RDC. Roblox Everywhere (standalone apps, web-native, console, offline) expands SAM; algo optimizations now balance LTV with monetization. O18 US users monetize 50%+ more than U18; 2D gaming and ad (pre-roll, Moments) rollout support diversified revenue. Near-term headwind: age-check communication restrictions dampening player interaction. RBLX +4.1% pre-market.

bullets.title: CHTR: Wolfe Downgrades to Underperform ($118 PT); MS Resumes at Equal-Weight ($150 PT)
bullets.body: Wolfe cuts CHTR to Underperform citing Starlink V3 (9x cost-per-Gb improvement, potential large price cuts), intensifying fiber competition, and ~$110B debt load limiting de-leveraging—'27-'28 looks even harder. Morgan Stanley simultaneously resumes at Equal-Weight, $150 PT (5x forward EV/EBITDA), crediting ~$1B each in opex/capex synergies from Cox but flagging thin equity layer and FWA/fiber headwinds. Cox mobile penetration gap (3% vs CHTR's 35%) cited as whitespace.

bullets.title: META: Muse AI Agent Launch Drives +2-5% Pre-Market; Commerce + Security Features Notable
bullets.body: Meta's Muse personal AI agent reached #2 in US App Store and includes 'Buy with Muse' commerce functionality. Security features include Muse Secure VM with Sentinel OS-level agent controls and planned Muse Confidential VM encrypting data with user-held keys. Multiple desks view Muse as a potential catalyst analogous to ChatGPT's launch for renewed AI enthusiasm, and as a structural differentiator in privacy/trust vs. competitors.

bullets.title: INTU: JPM Neutral Ahead of Investor Day; FY27 Growth Cut to 9-10% After Guidance Reset
bullets.body: JPM maintains Neutral on INTU; FY27 revenue growth guidance cut to 9-10% from prior 15-20% target after online paying customer growth slowed to 3% and TurboTax new customer adds stalled (75%+ additions from existing DIY upgrades). JPM expects investor day to focus on QuickBooks funnel and path to double-digit recovery; valuation at ~10x EV/FCF provides downside support but recovery duration unclear. Three Big Bets grew 34% and reached 30% of FY26 revenue—modest positive.

bullets.title: HUBS: JPM OW Ahead of Sept 17 UNBOUND Analyst Day; Margin Path Clearer Than Growth Recovery
bullets.body: JPM Overweight; expects UNBOUND to emphasize 200-300bps FY27 PF operating margin expansion toward 25% by 2028E, though growth recovery proof (new customer adds down to 5K-6K from 9K-10K) will lag. Over 55% of Pro+ customers using Breeze AI agents; deals >$120K ARR +38% y/y. Jefferies notes AI displacement risk but sees Breeze adoption as potential offset. Wells Fargo cut HUBS to equal-weight, $194 PT, on growth concerns.

bullets.title: TEAM: Mizuho Raises PT to $215 on 7-10% Cloud Price Increase + New Usage-Based Pricing
bullets.body: Mizuho raises TEAM PT to $215 from $175 (Outperform); cloud list prices rising ~7-10% with expanded usage-based pricing across Rovo credits, Automation steps, and AI agent resolutions launching Dec 3. A large channel partner estimates ~10% of customers could incur incremental charges at launch, rising materially through FY27. TEAM trades at 6.4x/5.7x CY26-27E EV/Sales and 21x/19.5x EV/FCF.

bullets.title: MU: Citi Bullish on Persistent Memory Undersupply Through 2028-31 from AI Continual Learning
bullets.body: Citi models HBM bit demand +62% YoY to 75.2bn Gb in 2027E and +69% in 2028E; DRAM demand grows +30%/+35% YoY vs supply +19%/+22%, creating -8.7%/-9.7% S/D deficit. NAND eSSDs demand +53%/+41% from Nvidia KV cache offloading; undersupply worsens through 2028 and persists into 2031. Top picks: MU, Samsung, SK Hynix, WDC/Sandisk. WDC separately announced redemption of $109.5M of 3.00% convertible notes due 2028.

bullets.title: PLTR: NVIDIA Running Supply Chain on Palantir Ontology; Government Wins Accelerating
bullets.body: Oppenheimer (Outperform, $200 PT) notes NVIDIA is running its supply chain on Palantir's Ontology platform; partnerships with Nebius, Fujitsu, and PwC expanding commercial reach. Government momentum includes FAA and L3Harris opportunities. JPM tech sketch also highlights Palantir's AIPCon 11 moat reinforcement and sovereignty demand acceleration.

bullets.title: CIEN: JPM Conference Takeaway—>$10B Backlog, 30%+ FY27 Growth Guided, Supply-Constrained
bullets.body: CIEN management guided FY27 baseline revenue growth of at least ~30% YoY, supply-constrained, with scale-across revenue in 'multiple hundreds of millions.' Backlog exits FY26 above $10B; gross margins at 45% with upside from data center product mix and value-based pricing. Management is returning to medium-term guidance—a meaningful confidence signal after pulling it a year ago. CIEN +8.9% on the week heading into Monday.

bullets.title: HPE: Evercore ISI Downgrades to In-Line from Outperform; $65 PT
bullets.body: Evercore ISI analyst Amit Daryanani downgraded HPE to in-line from outperform, citing valuation; $65 PT implies only ~5% upside from $62.09. HPE had surged +19.4% in the prior week (per S&P winners/losers tracker), making the downgrade price-based rather than fundamental. GS TMT also flagged HPE as a conference-week underperformer.

bullets.title: ACN: UBS Buy—Capgemini US Gov't Divestiture Creates Share Gain Opportunity
bullets.body: Capgemini is divesting its US Government Solutions business (~2% of US revenue) to ITC Federal due to French parent oversight constraints. UBS (Buy) sees ACN, with ~8% federal revenue exposure, as best-positioned to capture displaced market share. Separately, Wells Fargo cut ACN to equal-weight, $194 PT, on broader IT services demand concerns.

bullets.title: TXN: UBS Buy—Power Semi Beneficiary with Spare Capacity and New Market Exposure
bullets.body: UBS raises AI data-center power semis TAM to $13B by 2028E (vs. $11B prior), reaching $15B by 2030E. TXN (Buy) is preferred for PSU and IBC market share gains with spare capacity and products addressing new markets. Content per GW rises from $95M to $150-170M/GW. UBS is cautious on Infineon (Neutral) given high expectations; STM (Buy) also favored where power is upside.

bullets.title: IREN: JPM Upgrades to Overweight, $65 PT on Deal Momentum and NVIDIA Support
bullets.body: JPM upgrades IREN to Overweight with a $65 price target, citing deal momentum and NVIDIA support establishing IREN as a formidable neocloud player. JPM simultaneously downgrades CCI to Underweight (tower activity insufficient to offset Sprint churn) and MARA to Underweight (HPC strategy limits capital risk but also full value realization).

bullets.title: BE: Mizuho Raises PT 45% to $351 on Demand Visibility and Margin Signals
bullets.body: Mizuho raises Bloom Energy PT to $351 from $242 (maintained Outperform), citing stronger demand/pricing signals, higher ASPs, improving EBITDA margins, and better 2H26/2027 visibility. FLNC simultaneously cut 46% to $8 on slower AI/data center order conversion and extended deployment timelines.

bullets.title: FIG: KeyBanc Initiates at Sector Weight; Premium Valuation Justified but Margin Pressure Limits Upside
bullets.body: KeyBanc initiates Figma at Sector Weight; 690K paying customers (+50% YoY), non-designers now two-thirds of user base. Top-line growth expected to decelerate from 48% to mid-20%s in 2027, and gross margins fell steeply from 92%+ to 81.4% forecast for 2026 due to AI service costs. Trading at 6.6x 2027E revenue (136% premium to peers); analyst views premium as justified by platform position.

bullets.title: DKNG: SCOTUS Prediction-Market Showdown Looming; EBITDA Inflection 2027-2028
bullets.body: Hedgeye hosting a call on pending SCOTUS prediction-market litigation; states are winning recent legal cases on geofencing (Michigan, Washington), which could reshape the PM landscape and create a tailwind for traditional sportsbooks like DKNG by eliminating PM competition. Citi separately notes DKNG EBITDA inflection in prediction markets likely 2027-2028, with management constructive on handle growth and customer acquisition.
